title.narrative: Modernizing the National Statistical System in Tajikistan

description.narrative: The PDO is to enable the Agency for Statistics to modernize statistical production, dissemination, and improve user engagement.

The development objective of Modernizing the National Statistical System in Tajikistan Project is to enable the Agency for Statistics (AS) to modernize statistical production, dissemination, and improve user engagement. This project has three components. 1) The first component, Strengthening the Institutional Capacity of AS and Improving ICT Infrastructure, has the following sub-components: (i) Strengthening Institutional Capacity; and (ii) Improving ICT Infrastructure. 2) The second component, Enhancing the system of statistical production, dissemination and data use, has the following sub-components: (i) SNA-2008 and statistical infrastructure; and (ii) Electronic data collection and improvements in data dissemination and use. 3) The third component, Project Management, will finance operating costs, costs for goods and services needed for effective administration and supervision of the project by AS.

condition.narrative: Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I.A.1. The Recipient shall cause the Agency for Statistics to (i) ensure overallcoordination and implementation of the Project, and (ii) maintain, throughout the Project implementation, the followinginstitutional arrangements: (a) maintain, throughout the Project implementation, a Project Implementation Group with a structure,functions, responsibilities and adequate staff, all as further described in the Project Operational Manual (POM) and acceptable tothe Association, for the purposes of day-to-day Project management, monitoring, evaluation and supervision; (b) not later thanthree (3) months from Effective Date establish and thereafter maintain throughout the Project implementation, technical workinggroups to provide technical advice and expertise on issues related to the implementation of the Project, as further specified inthe POM; (c) maintain throughout the Project implementation the Inter-Agency Statistical Council (IASC) to ensure smoothcoordination between various public entities engaged in the Project implementation.

Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I.A.2. The Recipient shall cause the Agency for Statistics to: (a) carry out the Projectin accordance with the provisions set out in the POM; and (b) not amend, suspend, abrogate, repeal or waive any provision of saidPOM without the prior written approval of the Association, provided, however, that in case of any conflict between the provisionsset out in the POM and the provisions of this Agreement, the provisions of this Agreement shall prevail.

Increased traffic and data usage/download from AS official website

baseline.value: AS website having minimal features for: â€˜Open Dataâ€™ access; data download; and underlying data warehouse

target.value: Increased the number of downloads by 50%. At least 5 government agencies uploaded administrative and other datasets to the AS servers

actual.value: A new website platform was created, and its architecture was designed. The filling in the content of the pages of a website has not yet started. Currently, limited number of publications are available online on the website of the AS. The Bank team has recommended that AS places all its e-versions of its publications on its website. NADA platform has been developed but only few survey reports have been posted there, whereas this work requires comprehensive documentation of meta- and anonymized micro-data.

title.narrative: Increased traffic and data usage/download from AS official website

baseline.value: AS website having minimal features for: â€˜Open Dataâ€™ access; data download; and underlying data warehouse

target.value: Increased the number of downloads by 50%. At least 5 government agencies uploaded administrative and other datasets to the AS servers

actual.value: AS initiated conversations with the Open Data Watch company that leads the Open Data Inventory Index (ODIN). Since the launch of the new website in May 2024, one thousand files have been downloaded, to date 11 thousand files have been downloaded. To improve the open data indicator, a new web portal of the Statistics Agency has been developed within the framework of the project, for which for the first time a data dissemination calendar with the participation of TP experts have been prepared and posted. A license for open data was obtained and posted on the AS website after negotiations with Open Data Watch, and a section on the website â€œopen data portalâ€ was opened with a database on all sectors of the economy and social statistics. Assessment suggests that there has been significant improvement in the data-download volume under the new AS website compared to the old AS website.

title.narrative: Update of the Law on State Statistics, introduction of new Institutional Set-up and improved HR management system

baseline.value: Outdated Law on State Statistics, Institutional Set-up, outdated and inefficient HR management and HR policies

target.value: Updated Law on State Statistics is passed by the Parliament, new Institutional Set-up is approved by the Presidentâ€™s decree, modern HRMIS system is introduced, training and retraining plans are developed and being implemented

actual.value: The draft new law on State Statistics was prepared by support of TP legal experts. However, it was reviewed by WB and UNSD teams and specific recommendations were provided to adjust the draft so it can meet UNECE standard for statistics laws. The government advised that AS organizes an Inter-governmental working group to finalize the law and submit to the Parliament for passing. To that effect, by order of the Director of the AS, the WG was created on 01.07.2024 under No. 18 to revise the draft Law on Statistics. The first meeting of the WG was held on 05.07.2024. At present, the draft Law has been signed by all ministries and departments and submitted to the Government of the Republic of Tajikistan for consideration. No work on Institutional Set-Up has been initiated.

title.narrative: Number of UNSD Minimum List gender indicators available using data collected within the past 5 years

target.value: At least 50% improvement over the baseline value

actual.value: Latest review by the Bank confirmed that only 1/3 of UNSD Minimum List of Quantitative Gender Indicators are available . The project support organization of a Labor Force Survey in 2025, which shall help improve gender statistics in Tajikistan.

title.narrative: Number of UNSD Minimum List gender indicators available using data collected within the past 5 years

target.value: At least 50% improvement over the baseline value

actual.value: WB review showed that no specific database to meet the requirements of the UNSD on minimum list of gender gender indicators using the data collected within the past 5 years has been developed, despite several consultancies hired under the project to help with gender statistics. AS maintains a basic gender database (available at https://stat.tj/en/gender-database) that was created before the project, but it only contains about 35% or about 21 indicators from the UNSD list of 61 indicators using the data for the past 5 years.

title.narrative: Compilation and dissemination of national accounts using the concepts and definitions of 2008 SNA standard

baseline.value: National accounts compilation is in transition from using 1993 SNA to 2008 SNA with Economic statistics being compiled in cumulative periods

target.value: The general framework, concepts and definitions follows 2008 SNA standards with Economic statistics being compiled in discrete periods and SNA meeting at least level 4 of SNA 2008 standard

actual.value: Development of satellite accounts for tourism, improvement of the methodology for calculating the â€œnon-observed economyâ€ and application in GDP calculations. The calculations required for the SNA were carried out using the Gross Fixed Capital Formation and the commodity flow method, and the method was applied to the non-observable economy. Generally, progress on this indicator has been partial. Data for monthly GDP are still collected in sectoral departments on an accrual basis. The project envisages the transition to discrete period data collection which is necessary for full implementation of quarterly national accounts, which in its turn is a requirement of 2008 SNA. TP support was expected to be crucial on this, but WB assessments show that TPâ€™s support has been weak.

title.narrative: Compilation and dissemination of national accounts using the concepts and definitions of 2008 SNA standard

baseline.value: National accounts compilation is in transition from using 1993 SNA to 2008 SNA with Economic statistics being compiled in cumulative periods

target.value: The general framework, concepts and definitions follows 2008 SNA standards with Economic statistics being compiled in discrete periods and SNA meeting at least level 4 of SNA 2008 standard

actual.value: Progress on this indicator has been substantial., though the progress varies across components of SNA. The project envisages the transition to discrete period data collection which is necessary for full implementation of quarterly national accounts, which in its turn is a requirement of 2008 SNA. The Bank team agreed that PIG would hire two local consultants to support SNA 2008 transition work.

title.narrative: Shifting from paper-based household books to electronic ones in all jamoats

baseline.value: 31 jamoats (7.2% of all) use electronic household books

target.value: All jamoats use electronic household books. The national and regional databases are created automatically upon data entry at the AS server at 70% of jamoats.

actual.value: All jamoats were equiped with needed computers and data-entry program developed within the project. The system is connected to AS servers. Now, the problem is that a lot of jamoats are still using the paper-based household books because of internet connectivity issues. To help resolve this issue, the project agreed to support internet expenses in Jamoat offices for 2 years until project completion.

title.narrative: Data managed by AS has sufficient data privacy and security (physical and electronic) measures

baseline.value: Limited capacity to provide protection of primary data

target.value: AS has HW and SW for secure storage and subsequent archiving of surveys. Data having sensitive personal and private data â€“ both individuals and enterprises, are programmatically anonymized

actual.value: Security, insofar as the physical security of the HW/SW is good, but not enough. While AS waits for the parliamentary process that approves the data privacy regulations, there are certain technical measures that can be implemented, which are used internationally. A. Security for data in-transit. Data being sent to the AS Central Office from Regional Center, hubs, or data collected using online forms or via CAPI should use secure VPN (Virtual Private Network) channels and, if necessary a 2-factor authentication. I believe the VPN software has been procured. B. Admin Portal within the website that allows the Data Administrator to grant permissions to privileged users access to non-open data. Downloading of such data should be allowed only over VPN channels discussed above. C. Personal data of individuals and business enterprises. These data should be anonymized and/or obfuscated in storage before disseminating to privileged researchers and other users, who are authorized by AS to use

title.narrative: Number of anonymized survey micro-datasets available online

baseline.value: 0 â€“ number of survey micro-datasets available online

target.value: Number of survey micro-datasets available online is increased by 50% from baseline value

actual.value: To ensure access to microdata for scientific research and analysis in compliance with the requirements for the protection of primary statistical data and confidentiality, work is underway to document the surveys conducted in the updated NADA system installed in the AS. At present, metadata and anonymized microdata for 6 surveys conducted within the framework of the project have been uploaded and posted on the AS website, with a link to the dissemination system. Bank team recommended that AS also uploads relevant meta-data (various survey documentation, such as reports, questionnaires, sampling design notes, description of files and their variabes, etc.).
